description: UNESCO tracked the closure and reopening of schools and universities in every country during the COVID-19 pandemic, and the series is shared on the Humanitarian Data Exchange. The dataset page read on 2026-09-28 lists six resources: a daily CSV of closure status by country, a table of total closure durations as of March 2022, enrolment figures from the UNESCO Institute for Statistics, counts of affected learners, an additional education layer file and a methodological note on how closures and reopenings were tracked. The period runs from 16 February 2020 to 30 April 2022, and the update frequency is given as never, so the series is final. Coverage is global, by country, and UNESCO notes that more than 100 countries closed schools nationwide at the peak. Licence (read on 2026-09-29): CC-BY (HDX licence field: Creative Commons Attribution International). Access is free of charge. Caveats: status is recorded at national level, so local and partial closures are simplified, and definitions of full and partial closure follow UNESCO's note. It supports resilience studies of social infrastructure, such as measuring how long a pandemic disrupted education services and linking closure duration to learners affected. Related record: the Covasim epidemic model, which can simulate school closure policies.
